content.comment_body: I'm struggling with two main issues right now. I've attached the [document], which also includes explanations. 1. There is unexpected activity when powering on, even before the user presses START. 2. Pressing STOP doesn't reliably halt everything if timers are running; the STOP button only works when output Q1 or Q2 is currently switched on. Appreciate any assistance.
Would a solution like this work?

Thanks! However, I'd recommend not reorganizing things in that way. It makes it difficult to compare with the previous version and to see what's been changed. Additionally, now it won't start at all if i4 is active or if both i4 and i5 are active; it only starts when i5 is active. Are the M1 & M2 flags intended for a particular reason? These connections seem possible without using flags.
Hello, In [product_name] programming comparison is possible using [product_name] software. Open both versions and use the 'Compare' tool from the menu. Hope this is helpful.

Actually, aside from the inputs and outputs, the two programs are completely different. Using the comparison tool in [product_name] doesn't really make sense here. It might be better to review the programs first before recommending such steps.

That's correct. Typically, I don't insert outputs directly in the sequencer; I control them outside and use flags for recursion. But since outputs are placed directly in this small sequencer, flags aren't needed here. For your first issue, you are inverting the limit switch inputs at the NAND gates, so if the controller starts and a limit switch isn't on a '1' signal, the latching relay is set immediately, which starts the timer and activates the output. As for the STOP command, in your program it only affects latching on relays B004 and B005, not on relays B010 and B015.
